$comment: C 6.4.4.4 (D-CSUBSET-WIDE-HEX-OCTAL-ESCAPE-VALUE, CHARACTER half): a \x hex / \ooo octal escape in a wide/UTF character constant names a RAW CODE-UNIT VALUE and is assembled directly. This replaces a refusal that was itself repairing a SILENT MISCOMPILE (u'\xC3\xA9' once collapsed through the UTF-8 re-decoder into one wrong 0x00E9 unit), so the arms pin both hazards: a regression to the collapse OR back to the blanket refusal changes the exit code. The chosen values prove the escape is not a code point - u'\xD800' is a LONE SURROGATE, U'\xFFFFFFFF' is PAST U+10FFFF, u'\777' is octal above 255 - each MEASURED identical on gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51 (compiled and RUN, emitted unit read back, 2026-09-02). The wide STRING form still fails loud pending the semantic code-unit-count thread (see wide_string_hex_escape_error).

optimizedPipelines.label: release
optimizedPipelines.$comment: The escape values are folded at phase 5 and reach MIR as ordinary integer constants, so the shipped pipeline has no literal-decoding work to transform and the image is expected to match the baseline. Deliberately NOT given mustDifferFromBaseline - an honest no-op. The arm's value is that a constant-folding pass cannot quietly re-derive a unit the front end already got right.
